description: We develop technology-driven solutions for the next era of space exploration.
summary: ANALOGA (Analysis of Nodes of Analog Locations for Operations and Geology of Astro-terrestrial Environments)is a platform designed to identify, compare, and select terrestrial sites with potential as analogs for the Moon and Mars, intended to support training for future missions. It integrates a multifactorial comparison system (P.A.I.S.), a map of candidate sites in Argentina—identified using satellite imagery (SPA)—and deep learning models trained on thermal data from actual space missions. In addition to geological and environmental characteristics, ANALOGA assesses the legal viability of each site, indicating where research can be conducted and under what conditions.
details:
ANALOGA

Helps mission teams decide where on Earth to train for the Moon and Mars, bringing site comparison, satellite-based location, and thermal modeling into one platform.

P.A.I.S

The Planetary Analog Intercomparison System (P.A.I.S.) allows for the comparison of sites on Earth with those on the Moon and Mars across eleven key factors, ranging from geology and resources to the circadian rhythm of a crew. Once the comparison is complete, you can generate an easy-to-use analog report that is available for download.

S.P.A.

The Satellital Planetary Analog is an interactive exploratory map of analog sites in Argentina, identified using satellite imagery. Filter by Mars analog, Moon analog, or data collection site, and open a report for each location.

Thermal Models

An LSTM neural network trained on Curiosity REMS data from Gale Crater (Mars) that forecasts air and ground temperature one hour ahead, and a Diviner-based thermal reference for Shackleton Crater (Moon) that describes surface temperature across a typical lunar day. Together they define the thermal conditions an analog site needs to reproduce.
